RetailMax Holdings - Q2 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the RetailMax Holdings Q2 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss RetailMax Holdings' results for the second quarter. Joining me on today’s call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and David Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report RetailMax Holdings' performance for the second quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment of persistent inflation, softening consumer discretionary spending, and intensifying competition from e-commerce leaders.

In our roughly 1,200-store brick-and-mortar network, we've advanced significantly on our four-pillar framework encompassing store optimization, omnichannel acceleration, supply chain resilience, and customer-centric innovation. We've also sharpened our inventory strategies, managed markdown pressures thoughtfully, accelerated remodels for higher returns, and set a positive comp sales trajectory. These efforts underscore our resilience and focus on long-term shareholder value.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Mike. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the second quarter.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.75 billion, a 4.8% increase compared to the same period last year, reflecting resilient comp store sales of 4.2% and healthy digital growth. Gross margin was 37.4%, reflecting a balance of supply chain gains partially offset by elevated markdown activity amid softer demand in select categories. Operating expenses were $835 million, representing 30.4% of revenue, as we controlled SG&A while investing in strategic initiatives. Net income was $115 million, or $0.82 per share. We generated $220 million in cash flow from operations, supporting our balanced capital allocation. Inventory levels are currently well-controlled at 13.1 weeks of supply, down from 14.2 weeks entering the quarter, with turnover improving to 5.2 times.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

To give you more color on the drivers behind these results, let me expand on our key strategic initiatives, which continue to position us strongly in this dynamic retail landscape. As we navigate inflation pressures, declining discretionary spending, and competition from Amazon and Walmart, our efforts are centered on sustainable profitability and market share in physical retail. Across our four pillars—store optimization, omnichannel acceleration, supply chain resilience, and customer-centric innovation—we've seen meaningful progress.

On store optimization, we're advancing our Right Store, Right Market approach across our 1,200-store fleet. In Q2, we completed remodels on 120 locations, a 25% increase year-over-year, shifting to our next-generation MaxHub format with expanded high-margin areas like appliances and grocery adjacencies, drawing from models like Home Depot. These have yielded 14.2% comp sales lifts in the first 90 days, with traffic up 8% and average ticket up 5.3% from better merchandising and digital kiosks. Meanwhile, we closed 45 underperforming urban stores in high-rent areas like Chicago and San Francisco, where comps were negative 3.2% due to wage pressures; this lifted segment EBITDA margins by 210 basis points to 7.8%. Ahead, we'll open 15 small-format Express stores in suburban Southeast and Midwest markets by year-end, at 20,000 square feet each for quick fulfillment.

Regionally, the Sunbelt—including Texas, Florida, and the Carolinas—saw 9.1% comp growth from population shifts and housing starts at 1.45 million annualized. Northeast stores faced a 15% drop in consumer confidence but narrowed declines to 1.8% with fixture upgrades.

For omnichannel acceleration, buy-online-pick-up-in-store penetration reached 28% of digital orders, up from 22%, fueling 18% digital sales growth and 4.2% higher margins from lower last-mile costs of $3.50 per order versus $8.20 for delivery. Curbside MaxPick covers 85% of stores, tied to our app with 12.5 million users, up 32%, using Adobe tools for personalization; loyalty members spend 2.7 times more. In Canada, across 120 stores, BOPIS hit 35%, supporting 6.8% comps despite lumber softness.

Supply chain resilience has driven margin gains through a $45 million AI forecasting investment with Blue Yonder, cutting shrink 22% to 1.1% and boosting in-stock to 96.5% on core items like power tools. Direct Asia-Pacific sourcing is now 28% of volume, trimming COGS by 150 basis points, while new Mexico hubs cut Southwest transit by 12 days amid Red Sea issues—this fueled 90 basis points of gross margin expansion to 37.4%, above NRF averages.

Customer-centric innovation features our MaxGreen program with 15% sustainable SKUs like recycled paint and LEDs, appealing to 42% millennial traffic. MaxRewards membership grew 19% to 28 million, lifting repeats 15% and baskets 11%; RFID pilots in 200 stores cut out-of-stocks 30% and checkout times 40% with scan-and-go.

Overall, these track ahead with $320 million capex supporting 4-6% growth and 50-75 basis points EBITDA expansion. We're building a home solutions ecosystem, capitalizing on 60% in-store preference for big-ticket buys per McKinsey.

Building on that, our strategies for inventory optimization have been pivotal, enhancing margins, cash cycles, and omnichannel execution against e-commerce rivals. We improved turnover 22% year-over-year to 6.8 times, above the NRF's 5.2x average, cutting days outstanding to 52 from 68 and excess inventory by $145 million, avoiding $28 million in markdowns.

Core to this is SKU-level AI forecasting in our Oracle system, incorporating Google Trends, weather, and Conference Board data for 95% accuracy, up from 82%. This curbed apparel stockouts 35% last holiday amid hybrid work trends, adding 4.2% to comps; Southeast hurricane models cut overstock 18%, and Europe post-Brexit tweaks saved €12 million.

Just-in-time replenishment with VMI covers 65% of fast goods from P&G and Unilever, using POS data to shrink lead times to 7 days; ABC/XYZ analysis optimizes safety stock, boosting Nike footwear turns to 9.2x versus 7.1x industry. In APAC expansions, local VMI with Reliance cut costs 24%.

Omnichannel micro-fulfillment via AutoStore in 450 stores handles 72% same-day orders in 10-mile radii, lifting traffic 12% and cutting cross-dock inventory 40%; RFID on 80% apparel by Q4 ensures 95% cycle accuracy. Rural service levels hit 97.5%.

Dynamic pricing with PROS adjusts for velocity and comps, slashing clearance 27% and saving 210 margin points; Q2 outerwear cleared 92% in 30 days despite mild weather.

Geographically, urban North America turns at 7.5x, rural Midwest at 5.9x with pop-up DCs; Europe at 6.4x via private labels, APAC under 5% excess. FY24 targets 15% more turns with full RFID and AI scenarios, $85 million capex for $250 million savings and 3x ROI, beating Macy's and Kohl's.

Inventory now 18.5% of sales, down from 24%, bolstering guidance.

Relatedly, markdown activity rose to 18.2% of sales, up 210 basis points year-over-year from 16.1%, pressuring merchandise margin 140 basis points to 40.1% and overall gross to 37.4%, down 110 basis points. ASP fell 4.2%, apparel 6.1%, from entry inventory at 14.2 weeks, macro with 3.1% CPI and 1.2% income growth, and comps matching Amazon/Walmart on patio and apparel, where clearance topped 25%.

North America markdowns at 19.5% on warm weather and +1.2% comps; Europe 14.8% with +3.4% tourist comps; APAC 12.3% on premium decor demand.

Mitigations include AI dynamic pricing in 85% stores with Placer.ai and comp scans, cutting over-markdowns 15%; vendor penalties save 30 basis points; bi-weekly Value Vaults boost units 8%; BOPIS at 22% adds 200 bps margins.

Forward, private labels to 42% for 300 bps better margins, quick-response sourcing to 45-day leads, RFID planograms cut shrink 25%. Q3 markdowns 16.5-17.0%, gross 37.8-38.2%; FY at 37.5-38.0%, below NRF apparel 20.1%, with +2.5-3.5% comps.

Our store remodel and renovation plans are accelerating this momentum, fortifying our 150 million square foot portfolio of 1,200 stores averaging 120,000 square feet, 60% big-box and 40% urban. With $750 million FY24 capex, 65% or $487.5 million for remodels—up 35%—we're targeting 180 full remodels this year, 250 in FY25, prioritizing via Store Health Index on comps, leases, traffic, demographics.

Projects average 12-16 weeks, 1.2% comp drag; costs $2.6 million full, $800,000 refresh for 100 more, saved 12% via bulk deals.

OmniHub features AR/VR zones lifting tickets 18%; mobile POS cuts queues 45%, conversions to 34%; RFID shelves reduce shrink 22%; LEDs save $150K/store energy, EV chargers, green bonds.

Sunbelt (35%) adds fulfillment for +4.2% comps; Northeast/Midwest experiential for +1.1%; West Coast solar for 22% uplift; rural essentials lockers.

Post-remodel comps +17% initial, +12% Year 2; Q2's 45 stores +11% traffic, +8% units, 220 bps EBITDA to 9.8%. 24-month payback, 28% IRR, $1.2 billion incremental sales. Models 300 bps chain EBITDA by FY26.

Finally, on comp sales guidance, Q2's +4.2% beat +2-3% guide, sixth straight positive, with 2.1% traffic and 2.0% ticket on outdoor and essentials; margins up 110 bps to 38.2% from private labels at 28%.

Q3: +3.0-4.0%, lapping +5.1%; Northeast/Midwest +4-5% on remodels/RFID +15% conversions; Southeast +3.5-4.5% hurricane tools; West/Sunbelt +1.5-2.5% offset by BOPIS +22%. Hardlines +5%, softlines +1-2%.

FY25 raised to +3.5-4.5% from +2.5-3.5%, assuming 2% income growth, no tariffs on 35% imports. Tailwinds: AI planograms +8% comps, micro-DCs <2-hour BOPIS; counters grocery inflation, promos at 12%.

Longer-term, mid-single-digits into 2026 via store-within-store kitchen pods in $1.2T market.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Rivera, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines.

David Rivera, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our MaxGreen sustainable product line, featuring eco-sourced paints, LED fixtures, and outdoor essentials, which has seen exceptional uptake with sell-through 25% above plan and resonating strongly with millennials driving 42% of traffic. Early feedback shows 15% higher repeat purchases tied to MaxRewards integration. We are excited about the potential of this new line and other upcoming launches like expanded private-label hardlines.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions will be repeated. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation has been a persistent headwind, hovering around 3.1% CPI with real disposable income at just 1.2% growth, pushing consumers toward value. We've countered through targeted promotions holding depth to 12% of sales, omnichannel efficiencies like BOPIS at 28% penetration for higher margins, and category shifts to resilient hardlines growing 5%, which helped deliver our +4.2% comps despite softer apparel.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Emily. As detailed, Q3 comps are guided at +3.0% to +4.0%, balancing seasonal lapping while leveraging remodel lifts, BOPIS growth, and hardlines strength. Regionally, Northeast/Midwest at +4-5%, Southeast +3.5-4.5%. This supports our raised FY25 outlook of +3.5-4.5%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Alex. Our resilience pillar includes $45 million in AI forecasting with Blue Yonder, reducing shrink 22% to 1.1% and in-stock to 96.5%; direct sourcing up to 28% cutting COGS 150 bps; and Mexico hubs trimming transit 12 days. These drove 90 bps gross margin gains and underpin omnichannel like 72% same-day fulfillment.

Operator:
Thank you. As we have no further questions at this time, I'll turn the call back over to Mike Thompson for closing remarks.

Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.

aspect_summary.Strategies for inventory optimization: AI SKU forecasting (95% accuracy), JIT VMI (65% fast goods), ABC/XYZ analysis, AutoStore micro-fulfillment (72% same-day), RFID (80% apparel), dynamic pricing; turnover up 22% to 6.8x, excess inventory down $145M, avoiding $28M markdowns; FY24 target 15% higher turns.
aspect_summary.Markdown activity and its effect on marg: Markdowns at 18.2% of sales (up 210 bps YoY), pressuring merch margin 140 bps to 40.1% and gross margin 110 bps to 37.4%; mitigations: AI dynamic pricing (cut over-markdowns 15%), vendor penalties, Value Vaults; Q3 markdowns 16.5-17.0%, gross 37.8-38.2%; FY gross 37.5-38.0%.
aspect_summary.Store remodel and renovation plans: $750M FY24 capex (65% or $487.5M for 180 remodels, up 35% YoY; 250 in FY25); MaxHub format with AR/VR, RFID, LEDs; 14.2% comp lifts in first 90 days (+17% initial), traffic +11%, 24-month payback, 28% IRR; $2.6M per full remodel.
aspect_summary.Comp sales guidance for next quarter/yea: Q3: +3.0-4.0% (Northeast/Midwest +4-5%, Southeast +3.5-4.5%); FY25 raised to +3.5-4.5% (from +2.5-3.5%); mid-single-digits into 2026.
